title: Chain maps induce maps on explicit affine residue cycle quotients
statement: Let W be a scheme, U an open of W, p a prime ideal of A=Gamma(W,U), and K,C cochain complexes of module sheaves on the localized site. Construct their cycle quotients and projections qK,qC as in [lem-sc-affine-residue-cycle-class-quotient]. Let phi:K -> C be a chain map. Evaluate phi and tensor with kappa(p). The degree-one component sends cycles to cycles and boundaries to boundaries, hence induces an additive map H(phi):H(K) -> H(C). For every source cycle x, H(phi)(qK(x))=qC(phi1(x)). Both the map and cycle class are explicitly constructed, without any existence witness.

source.place: Tag 010V, induced homology map; Mathlib HomologicalComplex.Hom.comm, LinearMap.baseChange_comp and QuotientAddGroup.lift

proof.text: Evaluate the chain-map commutation equation with SheafOfModules.evaluation. Apply LinearMap.baseChange_comp to transport it to residue extensions. In degrees 1,2 it shows that phi1 sends cycles to cycles, defining the additive cycle map.

In degrees 0,1 the same equation gives phi1(dK01(y))=dC01(phi0(y)). Thus incoming boundaries map to incoming boundaries. Use the kernel formula for qC and QuotientAddGroup.lift to descend the cycle map to the quotients.
The defining equation of QuotientAddGroup.lift on a quotient class is reflexive, giving the displayed naturality formula.
